# Kukkuṭajātaka (Ja 383)

**ID:** Ja 383
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Kukkuṭajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul5.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kukkuṭajātaka* (Ja 383) is a birth-story preserved in the Jātaka collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya, opening with the verse incipit *Sucittapattacchadanā* [Fausböll 1883]. According to the narrative framework of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the Buddha delivered the tale while staying at Jetavana regarding a monk distressed by lust after seeing an adorned woman [Fausböll 1883].

In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta was born as a cock king (*kukkuṭarājā*) [Fausböll 1883]. A cat attempts to flatter the cock and promises to be his submissive wife in order to bring him under her power, but the cock discerns her deception and drives her away [Winternitz 1933]. Four verses narrate the fable of the cat and cock, followed by three didactic verses applying the moral: deceitful women behave like the cat, cajoling and bringing to ruin any man who falls under their sway [Winternitz 1933]. Maurice Winternitz notes that this narrative is depicted in ancient Buddhist sculptural illustration [Winternitz 1933].

 DharmaNexus reports Pali-internal text reuse with two parts of the commentary: ten matching segments with the third volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (up to 1,119 shared characters, longest segment §5.1–7.4 matching §2386–2393) and two matching segments with the fourth volume (330 characters, §5.4–7.4 matching §507–513), which contains Ja 448 [DharmaNexus].
